title: Northbeam Returns and Restocking: Calling a Return Off Before the Item Is Received
content:
The customer may withdraw a return only before the item has been received, and a withdrawal is recorded only against a collection request the customer has cancelled or an authorisation not yet booked in. Where the item is already with the carrier the retailer sends it back out and the schedule's reshipment fee is charged; where it has not left the customer nothing is charged. A withdrawn authorisation closes the line: the window is not extended by the time the authorisation was open, and a customer who changes their mind again raises a fresh return inside whatever window is left. A withdrawal does not count toward the profile's return history, because nothing came back. An authorisation the customer has stopped answering about is not withdrawn by the retailer; it is left open until the label expires and then refused.

## The position the authorisation must be in

On every Northbeam Returns and Restocking schedule the status of the authorisation and the day the item was booked in are read from the return authorisation record identified by its own reference number, before the withdrawal is recorded, rather than from the customer's account of where the item has got to. A withdrawal is recorded only where the authorisation stands requested, authorized or already withdrawn; an authorisation standing in transit, received, inspected, settled or denied is past the point at which a return may be called off.

## What the withdrawal costs

| Where the item is | What is charged |
| --- | --- |
| already with the carrier | the schedule's reshipment fee, the retailer sending the item back out |
| still with the customer | nothing |

## What a withdrawal leaves behind

- The line is closed. The return window is not extended by the time the authorisation stood open.
- A customer who changes their mind again raises a fresh return inside whatever window is left.
- The withdrawal does not count toward the profile's return history, because nothing came back.

## One situation the rule expressly does not treat as a withdrawal

An authorisation the customer has stopped answering about is not withdrawn by the retailer. It is left open until the label expires, and is refused then.
